cards.say: An LLM is built to produce text that is **likely**, not text that is **true**. When it doesn't know, it can still write a fluent guess. That's called a **hallucination**.

cards.q: Why can a model invent a source that looks real?
options: It writes plausible-sounding text rather than looking facts up
cards.why: It predicts likely-looking text. A citation-shaped string is likely, whether or not the paper exists.

sentences: The answer explains the idea in plain language.
The answer cites a very specific paper you can't find anywhere.
The answer says it's unsure and suggests checking a primary source.
cards.why: Precise-looking details you can't verify are a classic hallucination sign. Hedging and pointing to sources are healthier signs.

cards.q: Which habit most reduces made-up answers?
options: Give it the source text and ask it to answer from that
Ask the same question more forcefully
cards.why: Grounding the answer in text you provide gives the model facts to work from instead of guessing. This is the idea behind RAG.

cards.before: When it doesn't know, a model may write a fluent
cards.why: Fluent doesn't mean correct. Treat confident answers as claims to check.
